- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the middle of the horizon (days 10–20), often ignoring short-term volatility or policy-driven corrections.
- Model underreacts to strong downward trends in recent history — fails to adjust forecast downward when true outcome shows sharp declines.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true drop.
- Model overweights recent high prices in smoothing, leading to persistent overestimation even when true price is trending down.
- Forecasts are less accurate when true price exhibits strong mean reversion — model fails to recognize and adjust for reversion to prior levels.
- Model tends to overestimate volatility in the short term, leading to over-forecasting of price spikes followed by under-forecasting of corrections.
- Forecasts are more accurate when true price is stable or trending slowly — model performs better in low-volatility regimes.
